scope: Whether the executor can deliver an anchor aim at or near the latched onset, and whether the model's epoch band for campaign-night6-winner.json (fnv1a-be76035f) predicts the phone.
observed: An explicit NIGHT_ANCHOR_AIM_MS override is silently discarded when the anchor PERIOD cannot be looked up by winner hash. night-run.sh prints one 'anchor OFF' line and proceeds unanchored. The override is only honoured when NIGHT_ANCHOR_PERIOD_MS is also stated.
With the period stated, the anchor delivered aimMs 255 at lateMs 0.798 (origin.anchor status=released, k=1). Sub-millisecond delivery.
The model's band predicted the outcome. tools/device/epoch-scan.mjs scored epochs 400 and 450 at 0/200 for this winner, mostly Foxy; the run died at 167.8 s.

Band for fnv1a-be76035f, night 6, confirmed at 3000 seeds: epochs 0, 50, 100, 200, 250 and 300 all 3000/3000. Epoch 150 is 0/200 (Puppet) -- the 50 ms split-arming hole g263 -- and 350 and beyond lose to Foxy.

The effective-epoch relation was recovered from night6-anchor-aim-h-20260913.json: effective = aim + k*period + onsetBiasMs(-70) + input latency(47-82 ms, hall-lit). An aim derived from a winning band alone, without those two terms, is wrong by about 250 ms.

unknown.deliverableAimFloor: RETRACTED: the aim-0 slip was a disabled anchor, not a delivery floor. No floor has been measured.
unknown.night6TrackedAim: UNKNOWN(not-tested): the band implies about 255 for fnv1a-be76035f, but whether the executor delivers 255 is exactly what this run puts in doubt.
unknown.night6AnchoredBinding: UNTRACKED: binding h's aim fnv1a-37278c63 is registered but no tracked winner normalises to that hash; the winner file is part of the untracked-winner debt.
unknown.night6EffectiveEpoch: UNKNOWN(not-measured): converting a delivered aim into an effective epoch needs THIS binding's onsetBiasMs and input latency. Binding h's values (-70 ms, 47-82 ms) were borrowed for a derivation and the anchored run died at 107.7 s, consistent with landing outside the band. Those constants are priced for another policy and must be measured here.

retraction: The headline claim of this record -- that the device cannot deliver an aim at or near the onset -- is WITHDRAWN 2026-09-20, same day. The anchor was never ON in the run it was measured from. night-run.sh looks the anchor PERIOD up by winner hash even when an explicit NIGHT_ANCHOR_AIM_MS override is given, and the tracked Night 6 winner has no register entry, so the lookup failed and the script set NIGHT_ANCHOR_AIM_MS=off. Both the aim-0 run and a subsequent aim-255 run released UNANCHORED at a drawn phase (416 ms and 426 ms), which is why a 255 ms change in the request moved the delivered epoch by 10 ms. With NIGHT_ANCHOR_PERIOD_MS=5000 stated explicitly the anchor released at aimMs 255 with lateMs 0.798 -- sub-millisecond. The executor aims precisely; this record measured a disabled anchor and reported it as a hardware limit.
